registry.destinationResolver: Tenant owner binding: Build resolves the output repository from tenant_repository_bindings, not from a caller or a derived hash path
registry.note: repository name is derived from the live harness tenant id; no existing customer repository was written

chain: browser uploads a Package ZIP through the Capability wire (BFF /api/v2)
three-part replayed upload with idempotent completion; corrupt bytes and cross-tenant reads rejected
Runtime and WebUI admission, CreateBuild with three bound reference claims
real BuildKit composes one immutable OCI from the exact Package, Runtime and WebUI inputs
the composed OCI is pushed to the real Tencent TCR repository resolved from the Tenant binding
the worker reads the pushed manifest and blobs back from TCR to confirm identity
a ready CapabilityVersion is registered exactly once
Ledger persists both original domain events; lost ACKs replay without duplicates
worker SIGKILL after registry commit, recovered by a fresh worker with one artifact/event/version
browser publisher journey completes and reload readback preserves the same version

independentReadback.performedBy: separate registry HTTP read after the test, using the approved credential
independentReadback.interpretation: The artifact the Build owner confirmed is the artifact a later reader fetches from TCR; the worker did not merely trust the exporter.

defectRepaired.symptom: a real registry build composed and pushed its OCI, then never registered a ready CapabilityVersion
defectRepaired.rootCause: BuildKit pushed the manifest, but the worker reads blobs back through the registry, and Tencent TCR answers a blob GET with 307 to a presigned object-store URL. The worker rejected every redirect, so the readback failed and the job stayed needs_attention.
defectRepaired.fix: follow an approved redirect, bounded to a short chain and an approved scheme; Go drops the Authorization header on a cross-host redirect, so the presigned storage URL never receives the registry credential
defectRepaired.whyItMatters: without it, no real registry build can ever confirm its own output; the whole publish lane is unreachable on a real registry

liveLoopbackDefault.note: default harness stays loopback-only; no behaviour change without the opt-in env

notRun.reason: the local browser suite hung at 0% CPU for ~50 minutes in this sandbox; it is unrelated to this Go-only change. Source tests and the affected module were run instead. CI runs the full gate.

claimBoundary: A real end-to-end run of the Package upload -> BuildKit OCI -> push to a real Tencent TCR repository -> read the pushed bytes back chain, on an exact source commit, with an independent registry read confirming the same digest. Instance adoption and any production claim remain separate owner actions.
